# Why qmd-fast {.unnumbered}

**A fast, single-purpose dev server that turns `.qmd` files into live HTML — blog
posts, reveal.js slides, books, and whole websites — with executable code blocks
and an editing loop that updates the instant you save.**

qmd-fast is built around one idea: writing technical content should feel as
immediate as editing code. You save the file, and only the block you changed
re-renders — your scroll position, your live 3D canvas, your warm kernel all stay
exactly as they were. No cold start, no full-page flash, no waiting.

## Three things it gets right

- **Click-to-source.** Every rendered block remembers the line it came from.
  Alt-click (Option-click on Mac) anything in the preview to jump straight to its
  source, even across `{{< include >}}`d files.
- **Block-level incremental updates.** A save re-renders only the blocks that
  changed. Live canvases (Three.js, Observable) keep their runtime state; the
  page never reloads.
- **No per-edit startup cost.** A warm server and a warm Jupyter kernel mean
  edits show up immediately, and only the cells whose code actually changed
  re-run.

This guide is itself a multi-page **book** built with qmd-fast: sidebar, search
(press <kbd>Cmd/Ctrl-K</kbd>), live diagrams, and executed code cells included. A
companion book, [Internals](../internals/), covers how it works inside.

## Coming from Quarto or Jupyter?

qmd-fast reads the same `.qmd` syntax you already know, but it makes a different
trade: **do one thing — author HTML — and make the edit loop instant.**

- vs **Quarto**: no PDF/Word/format matrix and no `_metadata.yml` cascade, but a
  *live* block-incremental preview (Quarto re-renders the whole document), built-in
  click-to-source, and a warm kernel that never cold-starts on save. The config is
  a small subset of Quarto's, so your front matter mostly just works.
- vs **Jupyter**: you write in plain text files (versionable, diffable) with real
  prose, math, citations, and cross-references — not notebook JSON — while still
  getting live, cached, in-place code execution.

It is intentionally small: one author's HTML workflow, kept fast.

## Get running in 30 seconds

qmd-fast builds from source with a Rust toolchain (`cargo build --release`); a
`qmd-fast` launcher on your `PATH` then keeps the binary fresh and runs it from
anywhere. To execute code cells you also point it at a Jupyter kernel — see
[Executable content](using/code.qmd#code-cells).

```sh
# live preview, updating as you save (aliases: dev, serve)
cargo run -p qmd-fast-server -- preview post.qmd 4321

# build a self-contained HTML file (code cells are executed)
cargo run -p qmd-fast-server -- build post.qmd

# point either command at a directory to get a whole multi-page site
cargo run -p qmd-fast-server -- preview blog/
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:4321`, edit, and watch a single block update in place with
your scroll preserved. Add `--host` to expose it on your LAN with a QR code and
read the *live* preview on your phone.

One block model drives every output — a page, a slide deck, or a book:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  Q[".qmd"] --> BM["block model"]
  BM --> H["HTML page"]
  BM --> R["reveal.js deck"]
  BM --> K["book + TOC"]
```

## What it is (and isn't)

::: {.callout-note}
## Scope

qmd-fast renders to **HTML only** — there is no PDF path and no format matrix. It
is a focused tool for one author's writing workflow, not a general Quarto
replacement. The "spec" is a small corpus of real documents: when those render
correctly, the tool is done. That focus is the point — it stays fast, small, and
predictable.
:::

The rest of this guide tours what you can put on a page: [the live preview
loop](using/preview.qmd), [executable content](using/code.qmd) (Python/R cells,
Observable, 3D graphics), [rich writing](using/writing.qmd) (math, diagrams,
figures, citations), [slides, books and sites](using/formats.qmd), and the
[extension system](using/extensions.qmd). For how qmd-fast works inside, read the
companion [Internals](../internals/) book.
